strengths: Well-motivated problem: Identifies and formalizes the gap between appearance-driven and physics-aware V2A generation, with clear motivation and examples

Technically sound architecture: The Physics Parameter Estimator combines VLMs and dynamic 3D reconstruction thoughtfully; the Phy-Adapter's Δ-modulation mechanism elegantly integrates physics cues while preserving multimodal stability

Novel evaluation framework: VGG-Impact benchmark and APCC metric are principled contributions that move beyond semantic/temporal alignment to assess physics consistency; these will be valuable for future work

Comprehensive experimental validation: Comparison against 8 baselines, multiple metrics (distribution, perceptual, semantic, temporal, physical), user study with 4 dimensions, and convincing ablations (Table 3) demonstrating component contributions
Strong physics-grounded results: PAVAS achieves best APCC-Δ (0.378) vs. many baselines >0.5, directly validating the core physics-consistency claim
High-quality presentation: Well-structured paper with clear motivation, effective figures (particularly Figure 3 spectrograms), and detailed technical descriptions
User study validation: Demonstrates improvements not only on physics plausibility (4.34 vs. 3.96 for MMAudio) but also audio quality, semantic and temporal alignment
weaknesses: Oversimplified physics model: Only mass and velocity are modeled; critical material properties (elasticity, damping, friction, surface roughness) are omitted entirely, despite their importance in impact sound generation

Unvalidated physics parameter estimation: No ground-truth validation of mass/velocity estimates; claims of being comparable to specialist models [5, 66] cite other estimation methods, not ground truth. Monocular velocity has inherent scale ambiguity—failure modes not analyzed
Physics robustness not addressed: No sensitivity analysis showing how estimation errors propagate to audio quality. Missing analysis of failure cases when PPE fails
Limited benchmark: VGG-Impact contains only 272 impact moments across 10 classes—a small, manually curated subset prone to bias. Generalization to other sound types and datasets not evaluated

APCC metric limitations: Only measures correlation between kinetic energy and onset spectral strength; does not capture decay, timbre, spectral envelope, or other acoustic features. Based on single onset detection function; no statistical significance testing or confidence intervals

Incomplete physical validity: The assumption that spectral onset strength scales with kinetic energy is oversimplified; actual acoustic radiation depends on contact geometry, material impedance, and modal properties. No comparison with physics-based acoustic simulation

Incremental improvements on standard metrics: Gains on traditional V2A metrics (FD, IS, IB-score, DeSync) are modest compared to MMAudio. Raises question whether improvements are from physics conditioning or other factors (longer training, model size)

Experimental setup inconsistencies: Baselines use different sources (reproduced vs. author-provided) and evaluation conditions (16kHz vs. 44.1kHz for PAVAS). PAVAS advantage may be partly confounded with higher sampling rate

Architecture design choices lack justification: FiLM layers, Fourier feature mapping parameters (ωk), and learnable gates (αm, αv) appear somewhat arbitrary. No ablations comparing alternative conditioning mechanisms

Missing analysis and reproducibility: No visualization of learned modulation parameters or their correlation with physics. Code availability not mentioned. Two-stage training rationale not explained. Physics token dropout (p=0.1) impact not analyzed

Comprehensive experimental validation: comparisons against 9 baselines, thorough ablations, user study with 27 participants across 4 dimensions, robustness analyses
Novel benchmark (VGG-Impact) and metric (APCC) with robustness validation (inter-class shuffling 0.378→0.655; noise sensitivity analysis)
Physics estimation quality: mass ADE=6.954 (better than NeRF2Physics 8.730) with single-view input; velocity estimation outperforms SpatialVLM
Extensive supplementary material with implementation details, runtime profiling, missing-observation statistics, and generalization tests
Clear presentation of system architecture and thorough qualitative analysis via spectrograms showing improved temporal/spectral alignment

Narrow physics grounding despite title: only mass and velocity estimated (ignores material, elasticity, friction); no validation that generated audio obeys physics laws compared to simulators

strengths: Well-motivated problem: Identifies the important gap that existing V2A models are appearance-driven and ignore physical dynamics
Comprehensive experimental validation: Multiple datasets, metrics, baselines (9 SOTA models), user study (27 participants), ablations, and robustness tests
Novel benchmark and evaluation metric: VGG-Impact provides curated evaluation set, APCC metric is grounded in physics principles with demonstrated robustness
Thoughtful system design: ∆-modulation is more stable than direct summation; graceful fallback for missing physics cues via learnable occlusion tokens
Strong quantitative results on proposed metrics: Achieves lowest APCC-∆ (0.378 vs 0.536 for MMAudio), user study shows consistent improvements across all four dimensions
weaknesses: Limited core technical novelty: Physics Parameter Estimator is orchestration of existing models (Qwen2.5-VL, Grounded-SAM2, CUT3R); Phy-Adapter uses standard FiLM modulation with zero-initialized residuals; diffusion backbone from MMAudio. Contribution reduces to system engineering rather than methodological innovation

Physics estimation reliability is questionable: Mass estimation shows 82% APE on ABO benchmark; 3.55% invalid outputs on real data; velocity estimation has 65.15% of frames replaced with occlusion tokens due to SAM2 segmentation failures; evaluated on proxy benchmarks (STARSS23), not actual V2A data

Physics claims insufficiently validated: APCC metric measures only one physical quantity (kinetic energy) with oversimplified linear assumptions; no validation that APCC correlation corresponds to human perception; no ablation to isolate physics parameters from additional visual features (masks)

Incomplete evaluation: VGG-Impact has only 272 samples across 10 classes with manual filtering bias; user study on 8 videos with 27 participants lacks inter-rater agreement and significance testing; improvements on non-impact sounds smaller (Table S6), suggesting limited generalization

Physics modeling oversimplifications: Kinetic energy formula ignores deformation and heat dissipation; no handling of multi-object collisions or deformable objects; centroid-based velocity sensitive to segmentation errors; no validation of metric units

Unfair experimental comparison: PAVAS trained with additional pretrained models (VLM, segmentation, 3D reconstruction) vs MMAudio end-to-end; missing simpler baseline (physics parameters concatenated to visual features); parameter counts exclude pretrained encoders

Reproducibility concerns: Relies on black-box models with no code release mentioned; VLM prompting sensitive; no seed consistency or variance analysis; dynamic 3D reconstruction quality varies by scene
Limited scope and generalization: Only two physical quantities (mass, velocity); no material properties, damping, elasticity; improvements smaller on non-impact sounds; tested only on VGGSound domain

Missing failure mode analysis: No discussion of when method fails; robustness tests use synthetic perturbations not realistic errors; 65% velocity occlusion tokens not addressed; graceful fallback performance degradation not fully analyzed

strengths: Well-motivated problem addressing under-explored aspect of V2A generation: explicitly incorporating physics grounding rather than appearance-driven correlations

Robustness analysis demonstrating graceful degradation with perturbed physics estimates and effective handling of missing observations via occlusion tokens
